correctness.rationale: The only two-agent weighted envy comparisons reduce to signed integer imbalance x against the entitlement target alpha(p-q); both possible one-item corrections and their existence restrictions are enumerated. The re-encoded binary count Y=x+q has exactly binomial(m,1/2) layers. Inclusion and correction on two adjacent layers yield the finite formula. Hypergeometric endpoint bounds justify replacing qualifying layers by their full binomial mass asymptotically; Stirling and the local central limit theorem justify both regimes. A direct independent checker passed 315392 exact-rational assignment comparisons plus finite counting identities.

originality.rationale: Published closest results establish weighted mixed-manna WEF1 existence, algorithms, welfare, and entitlements but do not establish exact two-agent signed-unit WEF1 counts over all allocations, or the fixed-valuation random-allocation entropy transition. Random-valuation asymptotic existence is a different quantified question. No equivalent or stronger encompassing mathematical result was identified; this is a best-knowledge result with unindexed-enumeration risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed paper or generic two-agent balanced-partition census could imply this exact formula as a corollary.
The novelty of the elementary binomial transformations is limited; the contribution is their complete WEF1 phase and counting interpretation, not the probability theorems themselves.

value.rationale: Uniformly random allocations can be Pareto optimal yet almost never satisfy WEF1. The exact formula and signed-item/entitlement phase identify precisely when fairness rarity is polynomial rather than exponential, and exhibit zero-total profiles where the up-to-one relaxation collapses to exact fairness for every entitlement. The Gaussian crossover and arithmetic lattice factor quantify a natural implementation-robustness question not answered by existence algorithms; the work makes no claim of hardness or realistic prevalence outside its explicit model.
